title: Assurance Lab Probe Journal — SLO onboarding experiments
content:
Purpose:
This is a working notebook for fast experiments that inform our cross-functional reliability program and SLO onboarding pattern. Focus: cheap, reproducible probes that help product teams iterate on SLO definitions and observe real customer impact signals.

How to use this file:
- Iterate freely. This is intentionally messy — capture trial runs, quick commands, sample dashboards, failures injected, and follow-ups.
- Keep experiment entries dated. Tag owners and link PRs/jira for anything that graduates from toy to production.

---

1) Quick summary (what we learned so far)
- Many feature teams default to "availability" SLOs (p95 request latency < X) without capturing error semantics; leads to alert noise.
- Prefix/KV cache health and model-variant fallback are primary sources of production tail latency spikes (in hosted API experiments).
- Simple synthetic probes (end-to-end sample requests) catch config drift early but miss real query distribution — need blended synthetic + sampled real requests.

---

2) Experiment journal entries (chronological)

2026-08-12 — baseline probe (Marco)
- Goal: small-footprint synthetic probe for chat endpoint to test chaining fallback to smaller model variant.
- Steps run: curl POST to /v1/chat with sample conversation from customer QA set (seeded).
- Observed: fallback triggered 1.9% of requests during 30-minute stress window; latency 95th went from 210ms -> 780ms on fallback.
- Notes: need to capture fallback_count metric on per-route basis. Filed JIRA: SRE-678.

2026-08-16 — blended-sample trial (Sofia)
- Goal: evaluate representativeness of synthetic dataset vs. sampled real requests.
- Approach: sample 0.1% of production requests (anonymized) and replay them into a test tenant.
- Result: distribution of token lengths shifted right; 95th latency in replay cohort 30% higher than synthetic.
- Action: add a "sampled_real_beta" probe type to the lab and update admission checklist for SLOs to include at least one sampled-real-run.

2026-08-23 — oncall-runbook micro-alert (Kenji)
- Goal: reduce pager noise by shifting to multi-signal alerts: (error_rate > threshold) AND (tokenized_timeout_rate > x) OR (fallback_ratio > y).
- Experiment: implemented temporary composite alert in prod-sim and measured false positive rate across 72 hours.
- Observed: false positives dropped ~42% but time-to-detect regressed by ~6 minutes in one failure mode.
- Trade-off decision: keep composite but build a fast-path single-signal escalation for high-severity incidents.

---

3) Experimental patterns & templates (copy these into new probes)
- Probe metadata (required): owner, target_route, probe_type (synthetic|sampled_real|integration), sampling_rate, injected_failure (none|cpu|kv_eviction|network_delay), run_frequency, dashboard_link, jira_ticket.
- Measurement outputs (standard): p50,p90,p95,p99 latency, success_rate, fallback_ratio, error_breakdown, token_cost_estimate.
- Minimal acceptance criteria for graduating to "team SLO candidate" doc:
  - probe run for >= 72h and stable collection of metrics
  - evidence of production-like request distribution (either sample or documented deviation)
  - observed severity mapping (estimate of user impact windows correlated to probe failures)

Probe command example (toy):
- replay-sampler --source=sampled-requests/2026-08-15.json --target=test-tenant --concurrency=8 --observe-metrics 'prometheus:pushgateway/slo-lab'
- (We have a small python harness in the observability-probes repo — link above)

---

4) Cross-functional owner matrix (for SLO onboarding)
- Product/Feature team: defines customer-facing intent, acceptable user impact, target SLI definition, and business pri (SLO). Owner: PM.
- Platform/Serving Runtime: can provide performance envelope, caching behaviour, quantization constraints, and fallback variants. Owner: runtime eng lead.
- Observability (SRE): provides measurement harness, probe templates, alerting patterns, dashboards, and runbook stub. Owner: SRE lead.
- Solutions/Support: collects customer examples, impact narratives, and coordinates on incident comms. Owner: solutions lead.

---

5) Onboarding checklist (lightweight, experimental-stage)
- [ ] SLO intent doc (1 paragraph) with owner and business stake
- [ ] SLI definition (measurement window, aggregation method, sample rate)
- [ ] Probe run results (72h) attached + link to raw metrics
- [ ] Dashboard with top 5 metrics and alert preview
- [ ] Runbook stub with escalation path and rollback triggers
- [ ] Risk note: major dependencies (e.g., external model serving tiers, cross-region replication)

This checklist is intentionally terse so teams iterate quickly.

---

6) Failure injection ideas (cheap experiments)
- KV eviction storm: throttle TTLs and simulate cache churn on a small replica pool (non-prod). Measure cold-kv miss penalty across p95.
- Slow model variant: artificially add 200ms to variant B to simulate resource contention and measure fallback amplification.
- Partial region outage: toggle routing weights to reduce capacity in region and observe fallback traffic patterns.
- Tokenization attack: craft heavy-token bursts to see rate-limit and quota interactions (safety guard).

Caveat: all failure injections must be run in isolated test tenants or scheduled maintenance windows and must be approved by platform eng.

---

7) Short runbook sketch (for teams to adopt)
- Triggering conditions: sustained SLI breach for 3 minutes AND evidence of customer-facing errors (>=3 distinct customers).
- Immediate steps:
  1. Post to #sre-ops-slo with probe link + metrics snapshot.
  2. If fallback_ratio > 2% escalate to runtime oncall.
  3. If error_rate spike > 1% and leads to client 5xx, initiate rollback of last deployment on the route.
- Owners: product PM to confirm customer impact; runtime eng to perform mitigation.

---

8) Open questions / TODOs
- How do we standardize SLO windows across teams that have very different usage patterns (embedding vs chat vs batch)? Proposal: default to 7d rolling window for business-grade SLOs, 1h for alerting fast-paths. Need product alignment.
- What is the minimal sampling rate for replayed real requests to be useful? Initial estimate: 0.05–0.2% depending on traffic. Need statistical power calc.
- Can we build a 'probe-as-a-service' thin wrapper so product teams can self-schedule sample replays without SRE intervention? (Rough proto in GH PR above).

Immediate next steps (owner tags):
- @Marco: add fallback_count metric to per-route exporter (JIRA SRE-790). Due 2026-08-20.
- @Sofia: create sampled_real_beta probe guide and update onboarding checklist (PR to observability-probes). Due 2026-08-26.
- @Kenji: finalize composite-alert cadence and prepare oncall training snippet for SRE rotation. Due 2026-09-01.

Notes to self:
- Keep the lab small and instrumented; avoid turning this into another heavy program doc. The goal is to produce evidence that teams can use when they define SLOs.
- When a team wants 'final' SLO support, move the candidate through a 4-week pilot using these probes and then draft a formal SLO doc in Confluence.

Appendix: Useful snippets and links
- Quick grep for probe harness: github.com/redwood-inference/observability-probes (look at ./replay and ./prometheus-exporters)
- Slack threads: #sre-ops-slo, #runtime-fallbacks
- Related tickets: JIRA SRE-678 (baseline probe), SRE-790 (metrics), SRE-805 (composite alerts RFC)

End of notebook entry.

(If this lands in a runbook or playbook later, we should fold the checklist and 3-step runbook into the canonical SLO onboarding template.)
